mockups.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create a high-fidelity desktop web application UI mockup for OpenTriage's Review workspace. This is a proposed design with fictional sample data, not a screenshot of current data.
The attached Admin and Stationary screenshots are STYLE REFERENCES ONLY: preserve the existing app's visual language, but redesign the Review information architecture.
Exact visual system: full-width slim dark medical-green #00783a session bar, warm almost-white #fbfbf9 page background, white cards, subtle sage-gray #dedfd9 borders, light mint #e8f3ee active states, black #1a1c1a headings, muted gray #656962 secondary text. Inter/system sans typography. Flat readable professional clinical application, restrained shadows, 6–10 px corner radii, clear 44 px minimum controls. Avoid glossy effects, purple/blue dashboard styling, gradients, illustrations, oversized KPI tiles, excessive pill shapes, decorative devices, perspective, browser chrome, unreadable tiny text, dense text dumps, raw UUIDs.
Output a single straight-on landscape 1440-by-1080-like application screen, sharp and legible, filling the image edge to edge.
Keep the green session bar at the very top full width: small language and feedback outline icons on left, "Signed in as Demo" near middle, compact mode switch on right with "Mobile", "Stationary", "Admin", "Review" and Review selected white, followed by "Log out".
Below this, center a workspace about 1200px wide with 36px top spacing. A compact white heading panel says "Review" in 28px bold, "Demonstration EMS" below in muted text. On the right, a styled select "Synthetic records" and a secondary "Refresh" control, plus small "Updated just now" status.
Directly below heading use one cohesive HORIZONTAL main tab bar with these exact labels in this exact order: "Review queue", "Reports", "Analysis", "Retrospective", "Settings". Selected tab has mint background, green text, and a green bottom rule. Inactive tabs are neutral, no extra top-level navigation. Main tab controls look related to the reference Admin sidebar.
All text should be correctly spelled and readable. Do not put explanatory design annotations outside the app or duplicate navigation. Only display the chosen tab's content. Keep broad whitespace and hierarchy without wasting space.
Chosen tab: "Review queue".
Below tabs show three compact work filters: "Assigned to me  8" selected mint, "Unassigned  12", "All reviews  34". On the far right show restrained attention links "2 responses needed" and "1 reopened".
One compact filter row: search field "Search report or criterion", dropdown "All priorities", dropdown "Open reviews", outlined "More filters". No exposed bulk action controls until selection.
Below, split content 62% left and 38% right with 20px gap, in two aligned white panels.
Left panel heading "Your reviews" with small "8 open". A clear calm table/list with columns "Report & finding", "Priority", "Status". Five rows, generous 76px row heights; each uses a short familiar PCR number and a human-readable finding:
"PCR 2026-0142" / "Missing reassessment", High muted rust badge, "In review"; selected row pale mint with green left edge.
"PCR 2026-0138" / "Documentation completeness", Medium pale amber badge, "New".
"PCR 2026-0135" / "Medication reassessment", Medium badge, "Awaiting response".
"PCR 2026-0129" / "Unsigned report", Medium badge, "New".
"PCR 2026-0124" / "Documentation completeness", Low neutral sage badge, "New".
Subtle second-line "Today, 09:42 · Assigned to you" under first report; similarly light date/assignee information on other rows. Use readable labels instead of IDs. Footer "Showing 5 of 8" and discreet previous/next controls.
Right panel a selected review inspector, not a floating modal: small eyebrow "SELECTED REVIEW", heading "PCR 2026-0142", close X. Under heading "Missing reassessment" and "High priority · Assigned to you". A soft amber concise notice: "A follow-up observation is missing after treatment." Below small detail tabs "Summary" selected, "Discussion 2", "History". Summary has a tidy label-value list "Signed / Today, 09:42", "Clinician / Alex Morgan", "Criterion / Medication reassessment". A small "Open full report ↗" text link.
At bottom of inspector, clear labeled select "Review outcome" showing "Choose an outcome", a quiet outlined "Request response" button, and a prominent green "Complete review" button. Keep these contained with comfortable separation; nothing clipped.
The whole view feels actionable, friendly, modestly polished, recognizable as the reference app. No charts and no administration forms on this screen.

Left entries exact: "Assignment routing" selected, "Review outcomes", "Draft deadlines", "Amended reports", "Processing status". No dashboard metrics or charts.
Right white card heading "Assignment routing", small helper "Choose who receives new matching reviews." Below a table-like set of three clearly spaced routing rows with columns "Review criterion", "Assign to", "Independent review".
Row one: bold "Medication reassessment"; muted supporting label "High priority"; styled select displaying "Named reviewer"; a second labeled select below it showing "Alex Morgan"; checked square checkbox in independent column.
Row two: bold "Documentation completeness"; muted "Medium priority"; styled select "Unassigned queue"; unchecked square checkbox.
Row three: bold "Unsigned report"; muted "Overdue drafts"; styled select "Documenting clinician"; unchecked square checkbox.

Beneath rows, a soft mint information panel with small circled i icon and exact text "Independent review is assigned to someone other than the documenting clinician." One sentence, not a long policy dump.
Footer within the card uses a faint border and a horizontal action row: muted "Changes apply to future reviews." left, secondary "Cancel" and primary green "Save changes" right.
Below main card one small discreet white support card titled "Need to change review criteria?" with short helper "Manage criteria in the validation rule editor." and green text link "Open validation rules →".
The screen should be calm and exceptionally well aligned; settings not all expanded together. About 25% whitespace at bottom is fine. No overlay, no giant toggles, no excessive rounded chips.
